header: THE DATE OF BIRTH AND THE DATE OF JOINING, BY THE SEARCH BAR, FOR THE HOD OF C&IT ONLY (step 65b; my rule, 1 Nov 2026).

- a sentence that asks for one of those facts about a person who IS an employee (datesIntent.ts reads it; the people directory confirms the person) is answered ONLY when the person asking is the HOD of C&IT (SUPERADMIN_TICKETS, by the LOGIN's ticket; an authorised executive of the PAX editor is not the HOD and is refused like everybody else);
- everybody else, logged in or not, gets one plain sentence, and the database is not even asked for the dates;
- a sentence that is not about an employee (a circular about retirement benefits, an age limit) is not handled here: null, and the other routes answer as before.

I allow only THREE files to read the date columns (the others are query.ts, the lists, and employees/admin/store.ts, the employee manager, which hands the dates to the HOD of C&IT alone: its tests prove that an authorised executive never receives one, in the form, the search or the history); a test fails if any other file ever does. I use the application's own connection here (never the AI search's read-only role, which cannot see these columns anyway).

behaviours: ASKS: "${q}" -> ${want} about ${person}
NOT a question about somebody's dates: "${q}"
the HOD asks the date of birth of Anil Das: the headline is the date, written '01 Mar 1985'
...the table holds the name, the ticket, both dates
...and 'Understood as' says that only the HOD sees it
the date of joining: 02 Jun 2008
retirement: the last day of the month in which 60 is reached (born 14 Oct 1966 -> 31 Oct 2026)
'rakesh ojha' is two people in this fixture (RAKESH OJHA and RAKESH KUMAR OJHA: every typed word is a word of the name): the HOD gets both, not a guess
age on 31 Oct 2026 for a person born 1 Mar 1985: 41 years 7 months
service for a person who joined 2 Jun 2008: 18 years 4 months
two things asked: both are in the table, the first asked is the headline
by ticket number
two people of that name: '2 people', a table with both and the dates of each
a person with no dates on record: 'Not on record' (never a made-up date)

somebody who SAYS in the sentence that he is the HOD: nothing is shown and no date is read (the sentence is too long to be a name, so it is simply not answered; the HOD is the LOGIN's ticket, nothing typed)
${label}: ONE plain sentence ('${REFUSAL}'), no date anywhere in the answer
...and the DATES WERE NOT EVEN READ for ${label} (the database was asked who he is, never for the date)
a sentence about nobody here is not ours, for the HOD and for everybody else: the other routes answer as before
a sentence that is not about a person's dates is not ours (no database call at all)
a failing people search never breaks anything: null (the other routes go on), and no date is read
the HOD, and the dates cannot be read: a plain 'Not available', and nothing of the failure leaks
a common name: at most 8 are shown, and the dates of only those 8 are read
runOmnibar: the HOD's question is answered by this route (source tag, attempt 1), before the PAX route, the hospital route, the model and the model's client
runOmnibar: anybody else gets the refusal, from the same route, with the LOGIN's ticket (not anything typed)
a RETRY (a 'No' on an earlier answer) never runs this route again
a failing route never breaks the omnibar
an older caller without the dependency still works
a question about something else goes on to the PAX route as before (exactly one more call to it)
omnibar.ts wires the route to the application's own connection (getDb), to isSuperAdmin (the HOD, by ticket) and to the real people search
...never to the model's client
...the HOD is `isSuperAdmin(ticket)` and nothing else (the PAX editor's delegates are not the HOD)
...the route comes BEFORE the PAX route in runOmnibar, inside the block that a retry skips

ONLY THREE FILES of the program read the date columns: the lists (query.ts), this lookup (datesLookup.ts) and the employee manager's store (for the HOD alone); one more (api.ts) names them only in an error message. Any other file fails this test
...and api.ts, the one that only names them, contains no query (no SELECT, no FROM, no query call)
in the employee manager's store every date handed OUT sits behind the HOD-only flag: the record shows a date only when canSeeDates, and the history says 'hidden' unless canSeeDates
...and the handler passes that flag from the LOGIN's authority (hod), never from the request
the employee manager's panel reads no date column (it only shows what the server sent)
the AI search can never be shown these dates: the model's schema description does not name them
